## Big idea in one line

**AOP (Aspect-Oriented Programming)** lets you keep shared behavior — logging, timing, transactions, security checks — in one place (**aspect**), and apply it to many methods without copy-paste.  
Spring usually does this with a **proxy** around your bean.

```text
Without AOP                         With AOP
───────────                         ────────
OrderService.place()                OrderService.place()  ← clean business
  log...                              │
  time...                             ▼
  business                            Proxy
  log...                                ├─ log / time / security
                                        └─ real OrderService.place()
```

---

## Topic 1 — Cross-cutting concerns

A concern is “cross-cutting” when it cuts across many classes:

| Concern | Shows up in |
|---------|-------------|
| Logging | almost every service method |
| Timing | APIs / slow use-cases |
| Transactions | many service methods (`@Transactional` is AOP!) |
| Security | methods that need roles |

Filters/Interceptors help for **HTTP**.  
AOP helps for **any Spring bean method** (service layer especially).

---

## Topic 2 — Core vocabulary (simple)

```text
Aspect     = the class that holds the extra behavior (@Aspect)
Advice     = the actual code that runs (@Before, @Around, ...)
Join point = a moment you could plug into (method call in Spring AOP)
Pointcut   = expression choosing which join points
Proxy      = wrapper bean clients actually call
```

Mindmap:

```text
          @Aspect
             │
     ┌───────┴────────┐
 Pointcut          Advice
 "which methods?"  "what to run?"
             │
          Proxy applies both
             │
          Your @Service
```

---

## Topic 3 — Why proxies?

You ask Spring for `OrderService`.  
If an aspect applies, Spring may give you a **proxy object** that implements the same API:

```text
Client → orderService.place()
           │
           ▼
         Proxy
           ├─ run advice
           └─ call target.place() on real bean
```

**Important limitation (preview):** self-calls inside the same class (`this.otherMethod()`) do **not** go through the proxy, so advice may not run. Call through the injected bean/proxy instead. More in lecture 24.

---

## Topic 4 — Enable AOP in Boot

Dependency:

```xml
<dependency>
  <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
  <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-aop</artifactId>
</dependency>
```

That starter pulls AspectJ weaving support for Spring AOP proxies.

Mark the aspect as a bean:

```java
@Aspect
@Component
public class LoggingAspect {
    // advice methods in next lectures
}
```

`@Aspect` alone is not enough — it must also be a Spring bean (`@Component` or `@Bean`).

---

## Topic 5 — Tiny first taste (`@Before`)

```java
@Aspect
@Component
public class LoggingAspect {

    @Before("execution(* com.example.demo.service.*.*(..))")
    public void logBefore(JoinPoint joinPoint) {
        System.out.println("Calling: " + joinPoint.getSignature());
    }
}
```

Call any matching service method → log appears **without** editing that service.

We will unpack advice types and pointcuts in lectures 23–24.

---

## Picture: HTTP tools vs AOP

```text
HTTP request concerns     → Filter / Interceptor
Any bean method concerns  → Spring AOP aspect
DB transaction boundary   → @Transactional (AOP under the hood)
```

---

## Practice lab (IDE steps)

### Step 1 — Add starter

Add `spring-boot-starter-aop` to the POM; reload Maven.

### Step 2 — Aspect + `@Before`

1. Create `LoggingAspect` with `@Aspect` + `@Component`.  
2. Pointcut: all methods in your `service` package.  
3. Print method name in `@Before`.

### Step 3 — Prove it

Call a service method from a controller.  
You should see the aspect log, then business output — service class itself has no log lines.

### Step 4 — Remove starter temporarily (optional)

Comment out AOP starter / or the `@Aspect` bean → logs disappear. Confirms advice is not “magic in the service.”

---

## Short map to keep

```text
Cross-cutting = same extra logic in many places
Aspect holds that logic once
Spring AOP ≈ proxy around bean
starter-aop + @Aspect + @Component
Filters ≠ AOP (different layer)
```
